author: testing thread session (wrote the section, the prompts and the key)
observer: fresh subagent, started with this prompt alone; its hand-back recorded unedited
agent: general-purpose subagent, reads only its prompt

answers.why: There is an observable (response completion time) and an unambiguous oracle (elapsed time <= 2 seconds) under conditions the Requirements owner has said are specified.
answers.observable: Elapsed time from request to completed response, measured under the specified conditions.
answers.oracle: Pass if measured completion time is at most two seconds under those conditions, fail otherwise.
unresolved: The specified conditions must be defined concretely (load, hardware, payload), and whether the bound applies per response or at a percentile.

answers.why: Whether a Skill 'usefully' distinguishes Solution from Delivery, including ambiguity, is about fitness for purpose and soundness of a decision, so it can only be judged, not tested.
answers.evidence: The Skill's text and outputs on example statements, including ambiguous ones, plus how the distinction is used downstream by agents.
answers.judge: An Architecture owner or a qualified reviewer who weighs whether the distinction is useful and handles ambiguity soundly.
unresolved: What 'usefully' means in terms of purpose or consumers of the distinction.

answers.why: 'Sufficiently reliable' has no observable or threshold, so no defensible oracle exists. Requirements could make it decidable by stating a measure and target.
answers.question: What reliability measure (e.g. availability, failure rate, MTBF), what target value, over what period and under what conditions counts as 'sufficiently reliable'?
unresolved: Measure, threshold, time window and operating conditions are all undefined.

answers.why: The Case's pass criterion (an agent answers 'ambiguous') is observable, but its oracle rests only on the author's assertion that 'ambiguous' is right. Whether the statement is actually ambiguous (restrictive reading 'only the dishes that travel well' versus other readings, and Solution versus Delivery scope) is a question of soundness of the Case, which can only be judged.
answers.evidence: The statement itself and its plausible readings, e.g. whether 'only' scopes over the dishes served or the dishes that travel well, and whether it is a Solution constraint or a Delivery constraint. Also the Case author's rationale.
answers.judge: The Architecture owner or a qualified reviewer who weighs whether the statement is genuinely ambiguous and whether 'ambiguous' is a defensible expected answer.
unresolved: Is the statement genuinely ambiguous, or does it have one defensible reading?
Is the author's assertion alone an acceptable oracle?
